title: Mariner Insights - Retainer reshuffle & edge provisioning review
summary: Quarterly renewal/check-in focused on reshaping retainer tiers, adding EU edge nodes, and validating a small performance pilot. Customer emphasized data residency + KMS requirements. Redwood AE/SE walked through tiered capacity, canary rollout options and suggested benchmarking plan.
next_steps: Jordan to send amended SOW with three pricing tier options by 2028-06-06
Priya to run 95th percentile latency benchmark on customer's sample payload and share results by 2028-06-08
Ethan to attach SOC2 + KMS integration note and pointer to audit logs doc by 2028-06-04
Carlos to confirm procurement timeline and sign-off stakeholders by 2028-06-05
Schedule PI pilot kickoff (30 min) for week of 2028-06-11
action_items: Jordan: draft SOW amendment with EU-edge node pricing and burst capacity table (due 2028-06-06)
Priya: run 48-hour throughput/latency run at 2 load points (200 qps and 450 qps) and upload results (due 2028-06-08)
Ethan: compile KMS/HSM integration notes + example audit log exports and send to Ava (due 2028-06-04)
Carlos: collect final list of data residency requirements and confirm whether on-prem pilot needed (due 2028-06-05)
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-06-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim, Priya Nair, Ethan Park (Redwood) — Carlos Mendes, Sana Qureshi, Liam O'Riley, Ava Chen (Mariner Insights)

Summary (auto): quick recap of current usage, ask for a rebalanced retainer, and discuss EU edge provisioning plus security attachments. Agreed to run a short pilot for 95th pct latency with our quantized model stack.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): ok hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll run about 45 minutes, high level goal is to walk the retainer options and get agreement on next steps for EU edge provisioning 
[00:18] Carlos (Mariner): hey yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it. we've got a lot going on, late note — procurement's asking for a firm start date if we go ahead with the extra capacity
[00:32] Priya (Redwood SE): quick note from our side, we prepared three options: steady top-up, burst buffer, and hybrid reserved + burst. each has different cost/latency profiles and different lead times for provisioning EU-edge nodes 
[00:52] Sana (Mariner): lead times are a blocker — legal needs a month for amendments, procurement wants predictable cost. also KMS integration is non-negotiable for us 
[01:06] Ethan (Redwood CSM): we have a KMS/HSM playbook, we'll attach that. also audit logs are exportable per token call, token-level breakouts.
[01:25] Liam (Mariner SRE): tia, also curious about canary behaviour — how do you handle fallbacks if an EU node spikes or goes offline? 
[01:40] Priya: good q — we do smart routing by policy. primary region (eu-west) -> fallback to global hosted or a lower-cost quantized variant. during canary we route only X% of traffic and have an automatic rollback on latency/regression triggers 
[02:05] Carlos: What's the expected 95th latency delta if we move to EU-edge vs routing to hosted US? 
[02:21] Priya: in our tests, EU-edge typically cuts 95th from ~420ms to ~85-120ms depending on sequence lengths — assuming model variant is the same. if you use a quantized 4-bit profile you might add ~10-20ms but save TCO 
[02:41] Jordan: and for cost, hybrid reserved plus burst tends to be ~22% cheaper than fully hosted for steady high-throughput workloads because of batching & prefix cache efficiency 
[03:01] Sana: can you explain prefix cache again, transcription keeps saying kay-vee — not sure we got that phrasing right 
[03:12] Priya: sorry kay-vee is kv cache — key value cache for transformer kv states; prefix caching stores repeated initial sequences to avoid recomputing and that saves token compute for repeated prompts 
[03:32] Liam: any constraints around CCPA / data residency when using edge nodes? we need to keep PII within EU and redact tokens from logs 
[03:47] Ethan: you can enable token-redaction for logs, and we can write an S3 export that strips PII. we also support customer-managed KMS so keys never leave your control 
[04:05] Carlos: ok good. how about a small pilot — 2 weeks — to validate both latency and quality impact of quantization? 
[04:18] Priya: that works, we usually do a 10-day run, two load points and a small eval set of prompts to check quality regressions. we'll side-by-side compare full fp16 and 4-bit quantized variants 
[04:34] Jordan: timeline note — provisioning EU-edge nodes typically 7-12 business days once SOW is signed, unless you go private on-prem which adds more lead time 
[04:48] Sana: if we sign amendment by June 12, can you guarantee EU nodes online by end of month? 
[05:00] Priya: possible if we start provisioning immediately and don't need special procurement on the infra side. private on-prem would push it further 
[05:16] Ava (Procurement): on our side we need an SOW with line items: retainer qty, burst buffer, EU-edge monthly charge, and a cancellation clause for the start window — otherwise finance won't approve 
[05:32] Jordan: we'll draft an amendment that includes three price bands and clear provisioning lead times. we'll also include a rollback clause and canary gating metrics 
[05:47] Carlos: trials — curious about 95th P99 stability under sustained traffic. do you throttle? autoscale? 
[06:00] Priya: autoscaling for dedicated pools is policy-driven: we can scale on token latency or queue length. there's an optional burst buffer pool which is pre-warmed GPUs you can spin up quickly for short peaks 
[06:20] Liam: what about KV cache consistency across active nodes, like for chat session continuity? 
[06:32] Priya: we replicate KV cache for active sessions within the node group, but cross-region replication is eventual; for strict session continuity we'd recommend sticky routing (session affinity) 
[06:45] Jordan: also wanted to call out our Optimize tool — it will recommend batching sizes and quant profiles per route to meet unit-cost targets with latency constraints 
[07:00] Carlos: oh nice, can Optimize produce a cost delta if we switch to 4-bit for the assistant model? 
[07:09] Priya: yes, we can run a cost simulation with your traffic profile — that will be part of the pilot deliverables
[07:18] Sana: compliance: we need SOC2 + ISO certs and example audit logs. also we need to know where keys are stored if you manage them 
[07:31] Ethan: will attach SOC2 + ISO snapshot; for keys: if you use our KMS integration, keys are stored in your KMS (we support AWS KMS, Azure, and customer HSMs) — otherwise we have a managed option with full audit trails
[07:50] Carlos: procurement will want an amendment with indemnity language — will legal accept the standard Redwood clause? 
[08:02] Jordan: we have a standard enterprise addendum; we can flag the indemnity paragraph, but in practice it rarely blocks — we can loop in legal if you want to pre-review 
[08:18] Ava: yes please, send redlines we can take back to procurement 
[08:25] Priya: quick technical note on the pilot: we recommend two load points — steady 200 qps (current average) and an uplift test at 450 qps to test scaling and fallbacks. we'll collect 95th/99th PPL, token costs, and eval-set quality scores 
[08:48] Carlos: what's your method for measuring model-quality regressions? fuzzy match? human eval? 
[08:56] Priya: we run auto-evals (BLEU/ROUGE-type metrics for structured tasks) + a small human spot-check for hallucination/meaning. we'll set thresholds for auto rollback in the canary 
[09:14] Liam: how do you handle traffic mirroring? we don't want live user data going to a new model until it's validated 
[09:25] Priya: we can do shadowing (mirroring copies) with token redaction and sampling; mirrors are not returned to users and can be rate-limited to control costs 
[09:41] Jordan: ok let's confirm the ballpark numbers — you asked for an uplift from current 2M tokens/day to 5M tokens/day sustained? is that correct Carlos? 
[09:55] Carlos: yes that's our forecast, plus short bursts peaking at ~8M tokens/day during campaign windows 
[10:06] Priya: given that, hybrid reserved + burst is the best economics: reserved covers baseline and burst handles peaks. We'll show exact unit price delta in the SOW amendment 
[10:20] Sana: on billing, do you provide token-level cost breakdown by route/model and per-token granularity for audit? 
[10:31] Ethan: yes — Redwood Console exports token-level breakdown, per model & per route. we can also give a simplified monthly invoice view for finance 
[10:43] Carlos: any network egress cost implications for EU-edge nodes? 
[10:50] Jordan: egress charges follow cloud provider pricing; we'll list estimates in line items for each region in the SOW 
[11:02] Ava: payment terms — we prefer net 45 but can negotiate net 30 for retainer renewals 
[11:10] Jordan: standard is net 30 but open to negotiate in the AMENDMENT — we'll capture that in the draft 
[11:20] Sana: I want an explicit rollback SLA for canary — like auto rollback if eval metric drops >2% or 95th increases >50ms 
[11:31] Priya: we can codify those thresholds; we'll propose default gating and you can adjust 
[11:44] Carlos: what's the change-offer for dedicated vs private? dedicated is fine but private on-prem would remove egress and residency concerns if we go heavy on PII 
[11:58] Priya: private on-prem removes some concerns but adds provisioning time & ops overhead. we'd estimate ~8-10 weeks to get on-prem up depending on site readiness 
[12:12] Jordan: question for procurement — if we include an early-termination window for the new capacity, does that help your finance approval? 
[12:23] Ava: yes having a 30-day window post-activation helps reduce risk for finance 
[12:33] Jordan: ok we'll include a 30-day trial clause in the amendment for the EU-edge portion 
[12:41] Sana: one more on security: do you support SAML SSO + RBAC for console access? 
[12:49] Ethan: yes SAML, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC for routes/models. we can add auditors as read-only roles 
[12:59] Carlos: any pre-req from our infra for the pilot? 
[13:05] Priya: sample workload (JSON), a small eval prompt set, and a whitelist IP range for the edge nodes. if you want to mirror traffic we need a safe-redaction pipeline 
[13:20] Liam: we'll get the sample payload ready; also ask: does Redwood support model rollbacks per conversation id?
[13:31] Priya: yes, rollbacks can be per-route or per-conversation with sticky routing to the previous variant if you need it 
[13:42] Jordan: practical next steps: we'll draft the SOW amendment, attach security docs, and schedule a 30-min pilot kickoff once SOW is accepted. Are we aligned on that? 
[13:56] Carlos: yes aligned. quick ask — can you include an explicit cost comparison for 4-bit quant vs fp16 for our traffic? 
[14:07] Priya: yes that's part of the pilot deliverables; Optimize will give a simulation and we will run a short AB to confirm quality 
[14:18] Ava: send SOW redline to procurement alias procurement@mariner-insights.com and cc the legal counsel 
[14:27] Jordan: will do. any other blockers? 
[14:32] Sana: nothing else — just need final signoff dates from finance; we'll aim for June 12 sign date if SOW looks ok 
[14:41] Jordan: great. thanks all — we'll follow up with the SOW and attachments. 
[14:47] (crosstalk) Speaker 1: thank you everyone
[14:55] (end)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-heard acronyms (kay-vee -> kv), filler words left in. The team agreed to a pilot, pricing amendment, and security doc attachments.
